pattern.description: The navigation drawer snaps open over a dimmed dashboard, then the whole app window scales up about 1.5x toward the drawer while the cursor glides down the menu to Integration.
pattern.why_premium: Dimming plus a slow zoom isolates the one control that matters (the nav path to Integration), so a dense enterprise UI reads at a glance; the zoom lands as the narrator says 'importing', tying motion to speech.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.timeline().fromTo('.nav-drawer', {xPercent: -100}, {xPercent: 0, duration: 0.15, ease: 'power2.out'}).fromTo('.dim-overlay', {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 0.7, duration: 0.15}, '<').to('.app-window', {scale: 1.5, transformOrigin: '10% 40%', duration: 1.1, ease: 'power2.inOut'}, '<0.05').to('.cursor', {y: 260, duration: 0.8, ease: 'power1.inOut'}, '<0.2').to('.nav-item.integration', {backgroundColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.12)', duration: 0.1}, '>');
build_hint.remotion: Drawer translateX via interpolate(frame,[0,4],[-100,0]) %; overlay opacity interpolate(frame,[0,4],[0,0.7]); window scale = interpolate(spring({frame: frame-2, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 40, mass: 1}}),[0,1],[1,1.5]) with transformOrigin '10% 40%'; cursor y eased with Easing.inOut(Easing.quad) over ~24 frames; item highlight on arrival.

notes: Camera verdict is 'none'; the 1.5x scale is the app window element growing inside the frame (the blue background arc stays put), so the pattern is a simulated UI push-in, not a camera move. The energy spike at frame 498 is the drawer/overlay appearing almost instantly; the zoom follows over ~1 s. Pattern could also be read as cursor_guided_demo.
